problem.statement: The repository must use one coherent platform, partner, trusted-context, operational, and financial ownership model so actors and financial access cannot be routed through contradictory semantics.
problem.currentWorkaround: Individual capabilities may still infer platform semantics from service-local contracts or runtime configuration when the shared model is not consumed consistently.

permittedActions: read operational and authorized financial projections
forbiddenActions: mutate WLT financial truth through DSH
treat a partner or store as an operator or platform isolation context

actors.role: Operates authorized partner organizations and stores through embedded partner-management capabilities inside BThwani.
forbiddenActions: select or override platform isolation context

actors.role: Performs BThwani-affiliated or partner-affiliated delivery work.
forbiddenActions: change affiliation through an untrusted request context

actors.role: Performs authorized field onboarding, verification, and readiness work.
permittedActions: create and review authorized field evidence
forbiddenActions: override trusted platform or operator context

actors.role: Discovers stores, creates commerce intents, receives fulfillment, and views owned financial references.
permittedActions: request owned payment or refund workflows through DSH
forbiddenActions: supply trusted platform or operator context

actions: consume DSH commerce, fulfillment, and bounded financial projections
operate authorized partner resources through DSH
operate assigned fulfillment and consume bounded DSH financial projections
govern and operate through canonical owner facades
persist owner truth within service boundaries
reuse generated owner contracts and shared transports without parallel truth

outcome.statement: Every surface uses one coherent actor model, one platform isolation model, trusted operator-context semantics within that model, one operational owner per fact, one financial-truth owner, and embedded partner-management capabilities inside BThwani.
outcome.baselineState: Potential drift between platform-context terminology, service-local composition, generated-client provenance, and operational/financial access boundaries.
outcome.targetState: Zero in-scope semantic, trust, financial-access, provenance, contract-composition, and parallel-platform violations.
outcome.observationWindow: Every affected request, generated-contract check, targeted runtime smoke, and same-commit CI run.

criteria: Partner organizations and stores are business authorization scopes and never platform-isolation contexts.
Partner-management capabilities are embedded in the BThwani platform and operate through governed DSH, Identity, Workforce, Platform Control, and WLT boundaries.
All application financial access follows the current DSH-facing boundary and all authoritative financial mutation/truth remains in WLT.
Every registered generated bounded-context client is deterministically produced from its canonical composed contract rather than hand-authored as parallel truth.
Client-supplied context cannot authorize or override trusted platform/operator context.
Runtime and governance contain no separate tenant or partner-owned platform-isolation lifecycle.
failureStates: A surface calls WLT directly outside an explicitly registered application-facing exception.
A client controls trusted platform/operator context.
DSH calculates or mutates authoritative financial truth.
A generated client is hand-authored or stale relative to its canonical source.
A partner or store is represented as a platform-isolation context.
A runtime, contract, or governance source creates a parallel platform model for partner access.

business: BThwani is a unified multi-surface B2B2C commerce, fulfillment, and financial platform with embedded partner-management capabilities.
Platform Context is the platform isolation boundary defined by the canonical platform model.
Operator Context is a trusted operational/data context within the platform boundary and is not a Partner or Store scope.
DSH owns operational truth and the application-facing bounded financial projection/facade defined by current contracts.
WLT solely owns authoritative financial truth and financial mutation.
Captain affiliation is explicitly BTHWANI or PARTNER under the current model.
Trusted operator context is derived from trusted identity or server-side delegation.
negative: Partner Organization is not a platform or operator isolation context.
Store is not a platform or operator isolation context.
Partner access does not introduce a separate platform-isolation lifecycle.
Applications do not call WLT directly outside explicitly registered internal/owner boundaries.
DSH does not own ledger, wallet, payment, refund, settlement, payout, commission, or reconciliation truth.
Runtime environment flags cannot redefine the product model.
